_note: Every definition cites the file that defines it. Where the code does not define a term, the entry says so rather than guessing.

eval_q1_summary.csv.claim: Q1 — does the system improve end-to-end workflow time?
eval_q1_summary.csv.what: One row per trial: wall time, stall, and the arm it belongs to. The headline speedup table is built from this.
eval_q1_summary.csv.caution: Has no gpu_name. Facet using meta.json gpus[0] before comparing arms.

eval_q1_agg.csv.claim: Q1 — the aggregated speedup per arm.
eval_q1_agg.csv.what: Means and standard deviations per (workload, config, gpu). Now keyed by gpu_name so a hardware-pooled row cannot be emitted.
eval_q1_agg.csv.caution: This file produced every retracted speedup while it pooled GPU families. Pre-2026-08-30 copies are unfaceted.

eval_q2_breakdown.csv.claim: Q2 — where does the saved time come from?
eval_q2_breakdown.csv.what: Per-trial decomposition of wall time into load, stall, compute and overlap.

eval_q3_prediction_quality.csv.claim: Q3 — is the predictor any good?
eval_q3_prediction_quality.csv.what: Per-trial precision, recall, lead time and prediction counts.
eval_q3_prediction_quality.csv.caution: precision excludes failed and cancelled stagings from the denominator. A value of 1.0000 can mean 8 of 8 where most admissions failed and left the denominator entirely.

eval_q3_predictions_long.csv.claim: Q3 — one row per individual prediction.
eval_q3_predictions_long.csv.what: The long form behind the per-trial quality table; use it to audit a specific prediction.

eval_q4_speculation_cost.csv.claim: Q4 — what does speculation cost when wrong?
eval_q4_speculation_cost.csv.what: Wasted bytes, wasted seconds and cancelled work per trial.
eval_q4_speculation_cost.csv.caution: wasted_bytes is 0 for failed stagings because they carry no measured bytes — a failed prefetch costs time, not bandwidth.

eval_prefetch_lifecycle.csv.claim: Q2/Q4 — the life of every resource need: predicted, staged, hit or stalled.
eval_prefetch_lifecycle.csv.what: One row per (trial, resource) with the decision, the timing gates and the stall classification. The richest file here and the one behind the stall taxonomy.
eval_prefetch_lifecycle.csv.caution: One row per resource per trial, keyed on that resource's FIRST decision. A resource skipped then later started still shows the skip reason, so row counts are not decision counts.

eval_stall_taxonomy.csv.claim: Q2 — how much stall falls into each class, per arm.
eval_stall_taxonomy.csv.what: Aggregated exposed stall seconds by (workload, config, gpu_name, stall_class).
eval_stall_taxonomy.csv.caution: gpu_name is part of the aggregation key as of 2026-08-30. Earlier copies pooled L40S with Blackwell by construction.

stall_class.why: Classifies WHY a need stalled. This is the field that says whether a miss was the predictor's fault, the window's, or unavoidable.

values.baseline_no_prefetch: A need in an arm that never prefetches. The reference, not a failure.
values.no_prediction: The need happened and nothing ever predicted that resource. A predictor coverage gap.
values.no_window: The prediction arrived, but window_s was below the minimum — effectively at need time. There was no time to act.
values.window_too_small: A window existed but was shorter than transfer plus spin-up, so the need was unhideable however perfect the prediction.
values.late_start: The window was sufficient, but start_delay_s consumed it. A scheduling failure, not a prediction failure.
values.residual_partial: The transfer started early and finished after the need. Partially hidden.
values.gpu_serialization_residual: A vllm_model gate stalled even though the model's I/O was already done — the GPU, not the bytes, was the constraint.

outcome.source: scripts/extract_prefetch_lifecycle.py (row construction); values counted from the shipped CSV
outcome.why: What became of the staging attempt.

values.useful: Staged early and consumed by the need. The success case.
values.late: Staged, but finished after the need began.
values.duplicate: The resource was already resident; the staging was redundant. Counts toward consumption but is a scheduler dedup artifact, not a win.
values.failed: The staging attempt errored. On AtomAgents these are overwhelmingly 'Cannot start <model>: GPUs occupied' — the prefetcher colliding with its own prior placement.
values.skipped: A prediction existed but the scheduler declined to act on it.
values.cancelled: Killed in flight, usually by the divergence guard.
values.no_prediction: No prediction was made for this need.
values.no_prefetch_config: The arm does not prefetch at all.
values.direct_prefetch: Staged without going through the normal gate path.

decision_action.why: What the scheduler decided at the resource's FIRST decision point.

values.(blank): No decision recorded for this row.

decision_reason.why: Why the scheduler admitted or declined. The string names the gate that fired.

values.confidence_below_threshold (0.80 < 0.85): Declined. Note the arithmetic: the plan predictor's floor is 0.80 and the threshold is 0.85, so a plan-only prediction can never clear it.
values.naive_prefetch: Admitted because the arm bypasses the confidence gate entirely.
values.proactive_swap_compute_window: Admitted via the Tandem bypass — only fires when a residency actor is wired and can evict the GPU incumbent.

gate_group.why: Groups the rows belonging to one blocking event, so a single stall is not counted twice when several resources gate on it.

gate_on_demand.why: True when the resource was fetched reactively AT the moment of need rather than staged ahead. It is the direct negation of what the system is trying to achieve: an on-demand gate is a stall the prefetcher did not prevent.

values.False: A staging attempt preceded the need.
values.(blank): No gate recorded for this row.

gate_prefetch_scheduled.source: scripts/extract_prefetch_lifecycle.py:415 — direct = gate['prefetch_scheduled'] and not gate['on_demand']
gate_prefetch_scheduled.why: Whether a prefetch had been scheduled for the resource this gate was waiting on. Combined with gate_on_demand it separates 'we never tried' from 'we tried and were too late'.

window_s.why: Seconds between the prediction being actionable and the need arriving — the time available to hide the cost. The single most important quantity in this file: no window means no opportunity, whatever the predictor did.

start_delay_s.why: How long after the window opened the staging actually began. Large values with a sufficient window produce late_start.

completion_status.why: Terminal state of the staging task. Added because prefetch_completed is emitted for EVERY terminal state — including failure — and five consumers were reading the event as success without checking.

wall_time_s.why: End-to-end trial duration. The Q1 headline metric.

divergence_count.why: Times the agent ran a different tool than predicted, so the guard invalidated pending work.

values.note: Zero in every trial before commit 96f5f28 — the detector's semantics were inverted, so pre-fix zeros mean 'not recorded', not 'did not happen'.
